description.narrative: The Project will increase the supply of reliable electricity in Bhutan and enhance the countrys electricity exports to India, also resulting in a reduction of GHG emissions in India. The Royal Government of Bhutan (RGoB) is expected to strengthen its fiscal position through incremental revenues derived from transfers and taxation associated with the DHPP. The Project is expected to generate formal employment opportunities and support regional economic activity during both the construction and operating phase of the project in both Bhutan and India. The Project is also expected to contribute to increasing competitiveness by supporting private sector participation in Bhutans power sector.

The proposed Dorjilung Hydropower Project (DHPP, the Project) is a peaking run-of-river hydropower plant to be developed on the Kurichhu River in Eastern Bhutan. DHPP has a planned design capacity of 1,125 MW, expected annual energy generation of 4,504 GWh, and 12.6 million cubic meters of live storage, enabling peaking operation of up to eight hours. Power will be transmitted through a 35 km long, 400-kilovolt transmission line from Dorjilung to the pooling station at Durungri. Power generated from the project will be exported to India during the summer months, as well as consumed domestically during the winter months.
